clue.text: Frilly corsets for one hand-me-down

indicators.note: a corset tightly encloses the body, so one piece wraps around the other here

parts.note: frilly means lacy
for one means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Fancy lingerie, such as a corset, passed down from an older relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frilly corsets' paints underwear, but 'corsets' is a verb here: the frilly word wraps round the abbreviation for 'for one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something inherited from a predecessor, just as a hand-me-down is passed on from an earlier owner.

clue.text: Line on taxi mostly grease

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Uber is a ride-hailing taxi service

explanation.surface: A mechanic's instruction: draw a line of grease across the cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from UBER, the ride-hailing taxi firm, leaving UBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lube is short for lubricant, oil or grease that reduces friction between moving parts.

clue.text: Loves magic works, which may be Puccini

indicators.note: works as a verb means operates on or kneads, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves are OO

explanation.surface: Someone loves the magic of operatic works, perhaps those of Puccini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' reads as the operas but is the anagram signal for MAGIC plus OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo was the first name of the composer Puccini, so Puccini is one bearer of that forename.

clue.text: Lack cake decorating skills when receiving large number of churchgoers

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: someone who lacks cake decorating skills can't ice

explanation.surface: A churchgoing congregation is too big for anyone who can't ice a cake to cater for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large number' looks like one phrase but splits: 'large' gives L and 'number' (a song) starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant used in church services, so it is a musical number sung by worshippers.

clue.text: Make dashing leap, finally breaking cup sure to wobble

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece enters the other
letters set to wobble are unsteady and get rearranged
finally points to the last letter of the word leap

explanation.surface: A daredevil makes a dashing leap and smashes a teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wobble' scrambles CUP SURE into SRUCEUP; 'breaking' puts P (the end of 'leap') after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up someone is to smarten their appearance, making them look dapper.

clue.text: Stamping the time when teachers finally relax?

definitions.meaning: stamping a letter with the date and place of posting

definitions.text: the time when teachers finally relax?
definitions.meaning: a playful reading as ..., the period after the exam papers have been graded

explanation.surface: Teachers can only unwind once the marking is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmarking is the post office stamp franking mail; split as post-marking it means after grading.

clue.text: Warcraft from America's leader, but so refined

indicators.note: refined metal is reprocessed, so these letters are worked into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of America

explanation.surface: A boast that American warships, though led from the US, are very polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' looks like a compliment but is the anagram signal, rearranging A (America's first letter) with BUT SO.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines, vessels of war, so they count as warcraft.

clue.text: Former member of RAF moving one's milk

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: moving means one letter shifts to a new place within the word

parts.note: a pilot is a flying member of the Royal Air Force
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ex-airman shifts the milk he owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the one (I) a place along in the airman, giving PLOIT. 'milk' is a verb here, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk a situation is to exploit it, extracting all the advantage it offers.

clue.text: 2-D shape I'm not sure is for group of plants

parts.note: a polygon is a flat many-sided figure
um is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether a flat shape counts as a cluster of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygonum is a botanical genus, the knotweeds, so it names a group of related plants.

clue.text: Intelligence? Country that elected Bojo's losing it

indicators.note: losing means some letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: Boris Johnson, nicknamed Bojo, was elected Prime Minister of Britain, so Britain's

explanation.surface: A jibe that the nation which voted in Boris Johnson has lost its wits.
explanation.walkthrough: Bojo is the nickname of Boris Johnson, UK Prime Minister 2019-22; 'losing' drops IT from BRITAIN'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Brains is a common informal word for intellect or cleverness.

clue.text: Is French car maintaining parking rule?

parts.note: est is French for is

indicators.note: maintaining means holding or keeping within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Opel is a car maker and model
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Asking whether a French car keeps to the parking regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppel is a legal principle barring someone from going back on an earlier statement or position.

clue.text: Hornblower's hard on a corps pursuing gold coin

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the pieces it governs come after the coin
in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the word for hard comes last

parts.note: a louis is an old French gold coin
RM is the Royal Marines, a military corps
strong can mean hard, as in strong drink

explanation.surface: Reads like a naval tale: Hornblower hard on a body of marines chasing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hornblower' suggests C. S. Forester's naval hero Horatio Hornblower, but here it means a trumpeter. Royal Marines are the corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was a famous jazz trumpeter, someone who literally blew a horn.

clue.text: Give jobs to the boys? Time for a meeting

parts.note: giving the boys jobs is to appoint men

explanation.surface: An old-boy network handing out posts, then fixing a time to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment is an arranged meeting at a set time.

clue.text: What Victor may take, left in misery

parts.note: to the victor go the spoils, the booty of war
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A winner takes his prize and leaves the loser miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misery' is a noun for a gloomy person, not the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A misery, informally, is a grumbling killjoy who spoils others' fun, just like a spoilsport.

clue.text: Types info covered by journalist with Time

indicators.note: in a down clue, covered by means placed below the piece that follows

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor on a newspaper
gen is informal British slang for information
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Various kinds of information reported by a journalist for Time magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Subgenera are taxonomic ranks below genus, so they are kinds or categories of organisms.

clue.text: Use taser on left-leaning eccentric

indicators.note: in an across clue, leaning to the left means read from right to left

parts.note: nuts means crazy or eccentric

explanation.surface: Police tasering a mad left-wing activist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-leaning' sounds political but signals reading NUTS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A taser is a stun gun, firing an electric shock to incapacitate someone.

clue.text: A German with silver ra-ra skirts overturned jelly

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go around its edge, so one piece encloses the other
overturned in a down clue means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word ra-ra taken letter by letter, hyphen dropped
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A German woman in silver ra-ra skirts knocks over a bowl of jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: A ra-ra skirt is a short flared skirt from 1980s fashion. 'overturned' makes ARAR, which 'skirts' (wraps) AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used as a vegetarian setting agent.

clue.text: Honey bee caught in inlet

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea
B is the letter's spelt-out name, bee

explanation.surface: A honeybee trapped in a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' looks like bee produce, but it is the definition as an endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and baby are both affectionate terms of address for a loved one.

clue.text: Puts up stakes, fencing badly

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: stakes are bets placed in gambling
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone puts up fence posts, but makes a poor job of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stakes' and 'fencing' suggest posts and fences, but stakes are wagers here.
explanation.definitionFit: To billet soldiers is to lodge them, giving them accommodation, which is putting them up.

clue.text: Uproar at home? Smarten up the mess, say

parts.note: din means loud noise or uproar
in means at home
to groom is to smarten up

explanation.surface: A noisy row at home over who should tidy up the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like untidiness but is a military mess, where service members eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a room where military personnel eat together; a dining room is an example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Most slimy East German admits: 'You can't believe me'

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
you can't believe me because I lie

explanation.surface: A slippery East German confesses that he is untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily describes an ingratiating, unctuous manner, so the oiliest person is the slimiest.

clue.text: Piscine is rather cold

definitions.meaning: piscine means ..., read as the two words ...
somewhat aloof or distant in manner

explanation.surface: A fishy creature that seems rather chilly in temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs a split: piscine means 'of fish', which run together gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish is a variant of standoffish, describing someone cool and aloof towards others.

clue.text: Scatter articles of Spanish novelist

parts.note: el and la are the masculine and feminine forms of the in Spanish
F. Scott Fitzgerald was the American author of The Great Gatsby

explanation.surface: An instruction to strew Spanish items belonging to a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scatter' looks like a verb, maybe an anagram signal, but means one who scats: a jazz singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald was celebrated for scat singing, improvising wordless vocal syllables in jazz.

clue.text: Cockney is nowhere to be seen in time of putsch

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: someone nowhere to be seen hides

explanation.surface: A Londoner vanishes during a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March was the date Julius Caesar was assassinated in a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides, the middle of a Roman month, is when Caesar was murdered by conspirators.

clue.text: Setter heard vessel getting slap on the lid

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as spoken, by its sound

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: The compiler hears of a ship being given a slap on its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' is informal for make-up, and 'lid' for eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is cosmetic make-up applied along the eyelid.

clue.text: Fine soldiers knocking on walls

indicators.note: walls means encloses on all sides, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: knocking on is British slang for getting old, so aged
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers fined for banging on walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking on' is British slang for getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying fine to a proposal shows you consent to it, so fine is an exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: Maybe Oscar Wilde ate these when out to lunch

indicators.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy or confused, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde ate these delicacies when out dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' looks like a dining scene but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde was a leading figure of the Aesthetic movement, devoted to beauty and art for art's sake.

clue.text: Dry American statesman who led a coup

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A dry-humoured US politician who staged a coup.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was a Roman senator who led the plot to assassinate Julius Caesar.
